loyac-kilma-debate-program-nov-2026.about:
Kilma ('word') is LOYAC's long-running youth debate programme. Over three weeks of evening sessions (Sunday to Thursday, 5–8 pm Kuwait time), participants learn active listening, critical thinking, building and rebutting arguments, structured debate, research, body language and confident public speaking. Each session takes a different theme, such as persuasion, leadership or teamwork, through discussions of local and global issues and interactive activities.

The November 2026 edition runs from 1 to 19 November at LOYAC (Aisha School, Qibla) and the National Bank of Kuwait. The language of instruction is Arabic. At the end, participants form teams and compete in a friendly debate tournament to apply what they have learned. Past participants rate it 4.9/5 on LOYAC's portal.

LOYAC is a Kuwaiti non-profit founded in 2002 that runs leadership, volunteering and professional programmes for young people, with chapters in Jordan, Lebanon and Yemen. Kilma is a good first step for students who want to join school debate or MUN teams.
highlights: Three weeks of evening debate and public-speaking training in Arabic
Ends with a friendly team debate competition
Run by LOYAC, Kuwait's best-known youth development non-profit
loyac-kilma-debate-program-nov-2026.eligibility: Young people aged 13–17 who can follow sessions in Arabic and attend in person in Kuwait City.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the LOYAC application portal (apply.loyac.org) or the LOYAC app
Open the Kilma programme page and register
Pay the programme fee to confirm your seat
Attend all sessions from 1 to 19 November
loyac-kilma-debate-program-nov-2026.costs: KWD 70. Full refund if cancelled more than a week before the start, 50% in the final week, none after the programme begins.

loyac-kontinue-social-entrepreneurship-2.about:
Kontinue is LOYAC's social entrepreneurship programme for ambitious founders and early-stage startups. Over six intensive in-person weeks (Sunday to Wednesday, 5–9 pm, at Boursa Kuwait), participants learn to identify real user needs, write a value proposition, test the market, choose the right metrics and turn their idea into a workable business model, using established startup frameworks. Experts from different sectors run workshops on revenue, funding, legal basics and the founder mindset.

Each participant is paired one-to-one with a local entrepreneur as mentor for the whole programme, and teams are encouraged to build social impact into their ventures. The programme ends with a pitch of a viable MVP to a judging panel. Cash prizes are KWD 700 for first place, KWD 500 for second and KWD 300 for third. It is sponsored by Boursa Kuwait, Zain and Al Dau International Holding, and is taught in Arabic and English.

By the end, participants have a market-validated business idea that addresses a social challenge in Kuwait, an investor deck and a practised elevator pitch. It suits university students and young graduates who want structured support before applying to accelerators.
highlights: Six weeks of startup workshops at Boursa Kuwait
One-to-one mentor from Kuwait's founder community
Final MVP pitch with KWD 700 / 500 / 300 prizes
loyac-kontinue-social-entrepreneurship-2.eligibility: Ages 20–37 (LOYAC lists 20 and above) with a business idea that addresses a social challenge, fluent spoken and written Arabic and English, and able to attend every workshop in person in Kuwait.
how_to_apply: Register on the LOYAC portal (apply.loyac.org) for the Kontinue programme
Pay the refundable KWD 30 deposit
Attend all workshops and mentor meetings from 1 November
Build and test your MVP and pitch it on the final day
loyac-kontinue-social-entrepreneurship-2.costs: Free. A refundable deposit of KWD 30 is required and returned when you complete the programme.

loyac-darb-green-paid-internship-nov-202.about:
Darb Al-Akhdar ('the green path') is LOYAC's paid green-skills internship, sponsored by AGFUND and hosted by the Palms Agro Production Company (PAPCO), a listed Kuwaiti agriculture and landscaping firm. From 1 to 16 November participants work 9 am–3 pm at PAPCO's farm in Amghara (a bus is provided), learning about Kuwait's agricultural sector, plant varieties that grow locally, open-field and greenhouse cultivation, and plant care. From 17 to 19 November they move to LOYAC for an introduction to permaculture and design a sustainable space.

The programme also builds time management, leadership, teamwork and communication skills. A minimum of 80 of the 84 hours is required to receive the stipend and certificate, absences are limited to one day, and travel during the programme is not allowed. Applicants must not be employed, should be interested in sustainability, and must complete or register for LOYAC's Green Volunteering programme to receive the reward.

It is a rare paid, hands-on entry point into agriculture and sustainability work in the Gulf, and useful for students considering environmental science, agriculture or architecture.
highlights: Paid internship with a stipend and certificate
Hands-on farm and greenhouse work with PAPCO
Introduction to permaculture and sustainable design
loyac-darb-green-paid-internship-nov-202.eligibility: Ages 18–30 (portal lists 16–30), not currently employed, able to speak and understand Arabic and English (Arabic preferred), interested in the environment, and able to commit to the full schedule. Must pass a personal interview; university students bring their timetable.
how_to_apply: Register on the LOYAC portal and pay the non-refundable application fee
Receive an interview invitation by email and attend the interview at LOYAC
If accepted, pay the KWD 10 participation fee within two days
Complete at least 80 hours to receive the stipend and certificate
loyac-darb-green-paid-internship-nov-202.costs: Application fee KWD 2–3 (non-refundable) and KWD 10 participation fee after acceptance. Participants who complete the hours receive a paid stipend; transport to the farm is provided.

loyac-volunteering-saadati-nov-2026.about:
'Al-Tatawu Saadati' (Volunteering Is My Happiness) places young volunteers in partner centres for people with special needs across Kuwait. Volunteers act as teacher's assistants inside real classes, supporting students, encouraging participation and helping create a calm, friendly atmosphere. Shifts are morning or evening, 3–4 hours long, two days a week, and every volunteer must complete 16 hours within the month.

The programme aims to encourage young people to give back, build empathy, teamwork and communication skills, and promote social inclusion. A personal interview at LOYAC is compulsory before placement. It is taught and run bilingually (Arabic and English).

Volunteering hours with a recognised organisation such as LOYAC count towards LOYAC points and are useful evidence of community service for university applications and scholarships.
highlights: Hands-on volunteering with students with special needs
16 hours in one month, flexible morning or evening shifts
Bilingual programme with a compulsory interview
loyac-volunteering-saadati-nov-2026.eligibility: Young people aged 16 and above who can attend in person in Kuwait two days a week and pass a short interview.
how_to_apply: Register on the LOYAC portal (apply.loyac.org) and pay the KWD 15 fee
Attend the compulsory interview at LOYAC
Receive your centre and shift
Complete 16 volunteering hours between 8 November and 2 December
loyac-volunteering-saadati-nov-2026.costs: KWD 15 registration fee, fully refundable while registration is still open.

flex-global-bahrain-2027-28.about:
FLEX Global builds on the Future Leaders Exchange (FLEX) and the Kennedy-Lugar Youth Exchange and Study (YES) programmes and opens them to a wider set of countries. Funded by the U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs and implemented by American Councils with AFS-USA, Amideast and iEARN, it places secondary-school students with volunteer host families across the United States for one academic year. Participants attend a local high school, take part in community service and 'American Excellence' activities on entrepreneurship, technology, government and leadership, and act as cultural ambassadors for their country.

Bahrain is on the 2027-28 country list. Recruitment began in autumn 2026, results are announced in spring 2027, finalists travel to the U.S. in summer 2027 and return in May or June 2028. Selection is merit-based over several rounds, including English testing, essays and interviews; the programme looks mainly for students who can adapt and thrive in a new environment, not for native-level English. Placement is mostly in suburban and rural communities and cannot be chosen.

There is no fee: the programme covers travel, the host-family placement, school, insurance and a monthly allowance. Because the old YES programme for the Gulf has been paused, FLEX Global is currently the main fully funded U.S. high-school year open to Bahraini students.
highlights: Fully funded year at a U.S. high school with a host family
Bahrain is newly included for 2027–28
Merit-based selection; no fee and no agency needed
flex-global-bahrain-2027-28.eligibility: Citizens of Bahrain enrolled in secondary school who meet the age, grade and citizenship rules in the 2027-28 FLEX Global brochure. Applicants must not be U.S. citizens or permanent residents and must return home after the programme (J-1 visa). English is tested but native fluency is not required.
how_to_apply: Read the 2027-28 FLEX Global brochure on discoverflexglobal.org
Contact the Bahrain FLEX Global office (Amideast, flexBH@amideast.org, +965 9099 3374) to get the application link and deadline
Complete the online application and English test
Attend interviews and further selection rounds
Finalists are announced in spring and prepare for departure in summer 2027
flex-global-bahrain-2027-28.costs: Free. Airfare, host-family placement, U.S. school, health coverage and a monthly stipend are covered by the U.S. Department of State.

british-omani-society-arabic-language-sc.about:
The Arabic Language Scheme (ALS) is run by the British Omani Society with support from Oman's Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Each year it sends ten British students and graduates to the Sultan Qaboos College for Teaching Arabic to Non-Native Speakers in Manah, about 20 minutes from the historic city of Nizwa. The 2027 scheme runs from 6 June to 29 July 2027.

Participants receive five hours of Arabic tuition a day, mainly in Modern Standard Arabic, plus classes and language-exchange sessions in the Omani dialect. They live full-board in the college's student hostel in a fully Arabic-speaking environment, and the programme includes excursions to Oman's mountains, deserts and coast and to sites such as Nizwa. It is aimed at recent graduates and young professionals with at least mid-intermediate Arabic who want to reach a higher level and build links with Oman.

The scheme is fully funded: return UK–Oman flights, accommodation and meals, visa and insurance, and a weekly allowance for day-to-day costs. Successful applicants join the Society (GBP 25 a year) and become part of the BOS alumni network, which is a useful route into Gulf-focused careers in diplomacy, business and research.
highlights: Eight weeks of intensive Arabic in an all-Arabic setting
Fully funded: flights, full board, visa, insurance and allowance
Only ten places a year, with BOS alumni network afterwards
british-omani-society-arabic-language-sc.eligibility: UK passport holders with mid-intermediate Arabic or above (an academic foundation in Arabic), especially recent graduates and young professionals, with a genuine interest in Oman and the Gulf.
how_to_apply: Read the Arabic Language Scheme page on britishomani.org
Complete the online Arabic Language Scheme application form
Show your Arabic level and your interest in Oman and the region
Submit by 13 November 2026
If selected, join the British Omani Society (GBP 25) before travelling
british-omani-society-arabic-language-sc.costs: Fully funded: return flights, full-board hostel accommodation, visa, travel insurance and a weekly allowance. The only cost is BOS membership (GBP 25 a year).

otf-scale-oman-ideation-funding.about:
OTF Scale is the ideation-stage vehicle of the Oman Future Fund. It writes the first cheque, up to OMR 40,000, released against a first experiment agreed with the founder. No deck, traction or company is required at application: the fund looks for a clearly defined problem, a founding team with a reason to solve it and a first experiment it can fund. It is sector-agnostic, with a portfolio of more than 40 startups in fintech, mobility, tourism, edtech, climate tech, deep tech/AI and more.

The process is fast: a 15-minute application on the Oman Future Fund investee platform, a working session (not a pitch) with OTF Scale and its partner Al Jabr in week one, diligence and a 90-day experiment plan in weeks two to four, and an investment committee decision in weeks five to six. In return the fund takes a minority stake on standard early-stage terms, without board control.

Beyond capital, founders get help with incorporation, legal, finance, hiring and pricing during their first 180 days, introductions across Omani government and industry, and access to accelerator programmes run with Al Jabr, with a path to follow-on capital from the wider Oman Future Fund network. It is one of the few funds in the Gulf that will back a student or graduate founder at the idea stage.
highlights: Up to OMR 40,000 at idea stage, no deck or company needed
Decision in about six weeks; reply within two weeks
180 days of hands-on support plus accelerator access
otf-scale-oman-ideation-funding.eligibility: Founders building in Oman, founders willing to incorporate in Oman, and Omani founders abroad who want to return and build at home. Any sector. Students and recent graduates with a defined problem and team can apply.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the Oman Future Fund investee portal
Fill in the short OTF Scale form: the problem, why you, and what you would test first
Join a working session with OTF Scale and Al Jabr
Agree a 90-day experiment plan during diligence
Receive the investment committee decision and first funding
otf-scale-oman-ideation-funding.costs: No application fee. The fund takes a minority equity stake on standard early-stage terms.

startup-bahrain-pitch.about:
StartUp Bahrain Pitch is run by StartUp Bahrain, the national platform that promotes the Kingdom's startup ecosystem. Selected startups first take 'Raise: The Art of Fundraising', a two-week evening bootcamp (four-hour classes) delivered by Spring Venture Services, which is backed by Bahrain's Al-Waha Fund of Funds and Hambro Perks. Modules cover the global investment ecosystem, funding rounds, equity crowdfunding, pitching to investors, key investment documents, data rooms, valuation, product-market fit and exit strategies, with hands-on workshops, fireside chats and one-to-one office hours.

The programme ends with a pitch night: each shortlisted startup pitches for several minutes and answers judges' questions in front of an audience, and the winner receives a cash prize released against milestones, with possible further support from partners. Past judges have included investors from Spring, MEVP, Shorooq and AWS.

It suits student and graduate founders who already have a minimum viable product and a registered company in Bahrain. StartUp Bahrain also runs the three-day StartUp Bahrain Weekend for people who are still at the idea stage (the 2026 edition was held in May with the University of Bahrain).
highlights: Two-week fundraising bootcamp with Spring Venture Services
Pitch to leading Gulf VCs for a milestone-based cash prize
Free to apply; applications reviewed manually
startup-bahrain-pitch.eligibility: Bahrain-based startups with a Commercial Registration (CR), a minimum viable product, a scalable and innovative product relevant to the local or regional market, and at least one Bahraini founder.
how_to_apply: Prepare your startup details: CR, stage, revenue, product, customers and team
Fill in the application form on startupbahrain.com/pitch
Wait for the manual review and acceptance email
Complete the two-week bootcamp
Pitch at the final event
startup-bahrain-pitch.costs: Free to apply and take part.

edraak-arabic-online-courses.about:
Edraak is a massive open online course (MOOC) platform launched by the Queen Rania Foundation for Education and Development in Jordan, built on technology developed by the Harvard–MIT consortium edX. Its aim is to bring high-quality learning to Arabic speakers: original Arabic courses from leading Arab professors and practitioners, and Arabic access to courses from institutions such as HarvardX, MITx and BerkeleyX.

Today the catalogue is organised into career readiness, technology, personal development, business and entrepreneurship, and languages, with multi-course 'specialisations' and a separate K-12 education platform for school students. Courses are self-paced and can be followed on the web or the Edraak mobile app.

For students in Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman and the rest of the region it is an easy, free way to build skills in Arabic, prepare for university or the job market, and earn course certificates to show on CVs and applications. Check each course page for whether a certificate is free or paid.
highlights: Free, self-paced courses in Arabic from a non-profit
Career readiness, tech, business, languages and a K-12 platform
Web and mobile app; certificates on completion
edraak-arabic-online-courses.eligibility: Anyone, anywhere, who can learn in Arabic. Free registration with an email address. Separate K-12 content for school students.
how_to_apply: Go to edraak.org and click 'Register for Free'
Browse categories or specialisations
Enrol in a course and study at your own pace on the web or app
Complete assessments to earn a certificate where offered
edraak-arabic-online-courses.costs: Courses are free to the learner; some certificates or specialisations may carry a fee, shown on each course page.

world-scholars-cup-kuwait-round-2026.about:
The World Scholar's Cup (WSC) is a not-for-profit international academic programme for students aged about 10 to 18. Each season has one interdisciplinary theme (the 2026 theme is 'Are We There Yet?') with study guides across history, social studies, science and technology, art and music, literature and a special area. At each round, teams of three compete in four events: Team Debate, Collaborative Writing, the Scholar's Challenge (a multiple-choice test) and the Scholar's Bowl, a team quiz in a theatre with clickers.

The Kuwait Round takes place on 6–7 November 2026 at Al Nibras International Bilingual School. There are two divisions: juniors (up to 13) and seniors (14 and over, up to the final year of secondary school). Students can register as a school team, form mixed teams with students from other schools, or register individually and be matched with teammates. Most teams prepare for two to eight weeks. Teams that reach the qualifying threshold earn places at the Global Rounds (held June to August) and then at the Tournament of Champions at Yale University in November.

WSC is designed to reach well beyond a school's top three students, and it is a fun way to build debating, writing and research skills in English, meet students from across Kuwait and the region, and earn international medals. All study materials are free; each round charges a modest tournament fee that usually includes meals.
highlights: Four events: debate, collaborative writing, quiz bowl and scholar's challenge
Path to Global Rounds and the Tournament of Champions at Yale
Teams of three; individuals can be matched with teammates
world-scholars-cup-kuwait-round-2026.eligibility: Students aged about 10–18 from any school in Kuwait or abroad, in junior (up to 13) or senior (14+, until the last year of pre-university schooling) divisions. A team may compete in only one regional round per season. Events are in English.
how_to_apply: Form a team of three (or register individually to be matched)
Register through the online registration link on the Kuwait Round page
Download the 2026 theme and curriculum guides from scholarscup.org and prepare
Attend both days at Al Nibras International Bilingual School
Check results to see whether you qualified for a Global Round
world-scholars-cup-kuwait-round-2026.costs: Study materials are free. A tournament fee applies per participant (set by round, usually including meals); see the registration page. Global Round travel is paid by participants.

coded-kuwait-codes.about:
Kuwait Codes is a non-profit initiative powered by CODED, Kuwait's coding academy (founded in 2015 and describing itself as the first coding academy in the Arab world). It gives high-school students free, hands-on tech and AI education, funded by corporate partners and sponsors. Each cohort lasts two weeks, in person at the CODED campus in Kuwait's Free Trade Zone, and no prior experience is needed.

Students choose one track: Python with AI (coding alongside modern AI tools and building simple AI-powered apps), Web with AI (how modern websites are built, from layout to interactivity, using AI to design, code and ship a site) or Cybersecurity (core concepts and real tools, finishing with a Capture The Flag challenge). Every team ships a working project and presents it to instructors, guests and partners on demo day, and students graduate with a measurable outcome.

Since February 2025 Kuwait Codes has run six cohorts and received more than 6,400 applications, so places are competitive. It is a strong, free starting point for students considering computer science, engineering or cybersecurity, and the project gives something concrete to show on university applications.
highlights: Completely free and fully sponsored
Tracks in Python with AI, Web with AI and Cybersecurity (with a CTF)
Ends with a live project demo
coded-kuwait-codes.eligibility: High-school students in grades 9–12 (ages 14–18) who can attend in person in Kuwait. Beginners welcome; check the cohort page for the teaching language.
how_to_apply: Open the Kuwait Codes page on coded.kw
Join the waitlist to get the next cohort dates first
Apply when the cohort opens and choose one track
Attend all sessions for two weeks and present your project on demo day

coded-academy-x-girls.about:
Academy X is CODED's non-profit, girls-only programme to build real capability in technology, entrepreneurship and marketing. Over two weeks of in-person, hands-on workshops at the CODED campus, participants learn UI/UX design, AI tools, digital marketing and tech entrepreneurship: validating a problem, designing a solution, building a working prototype and pitching like a founder. A 'Marketing with AI' track covers content creation, campaigns and performance analysis with AI.

Students work in teams and finish by presenting their project to instructors, guests and partners for feedback and recognition. Sessions are delivered by female instructors in a supportive, women-only environment. Since January 2025 Academy X has run four cohorts and trained more than 450 high-school and university girls.

It is entirely free, supported by CODED's partners and sponsors, and suits any girl curious about startups, design or marketing, whatever she studies (past participants include medical students).
highlights: Free and girls-only, taught by female instructors
UI/UX, AI tools, marketing and entrepreneurship
Ends with a team project pitch
coded-academy-x-girls.eligibility: Girls in high school or university in Kuwait who can attend in person. No prior experience needed.
how_to_apply: Open the Academy X page on coded.kw
Join the waitlist to hear about the next cohort first
Apply when registration opens
Attend the two weeks of workshops and pitch your project

coded-ai-app-developer-bootcamp-nov-2026.about:
CODED's AI App Developer bootcamp takes participants from an idea to a live, working application in five weeks. Classes run on Sunday, Tuesday and Thursday evenings (4:30–7:30 pm) at the CODED campus in Kuwait's Free Trade Zone, from 29 November to 31 December 2026. It is beginner-friendly: the focus is on directing AI tools with intention and understanding systems, not memorising syntax.

The six modules cover: the AI app foundation (structuring an idea, user flows, AI-generated interfaces and a first live deployment); connecting to real services and APIs; designing a data system with a live database; securing the app with authentication and role-based access; launching with payments, a custom domain, analytics and user testing; and a capstone week in which each participant designs, builds and launches a complete AI-powered app independently and presents it.

CODED has trained more than 10,000 graduates since 2015. The bootcamp suits university students, graduates and young professionals who want to ship their own product or startup MVP quickly.
highlights: From idea to a live AI-powered app in five weeks
APIs, databases, authentication, payments and deployment
Beginner-friendly, evening schedule
coded-ai-app-developer-bootcamp-nov-2026.eligibility: Adults and university students in Kuwait who can attend evening classes in person. No coding background required.
how_to_apply: Open the AI App Developer page on coded.kw
Click 'Apply Now' and submit the form
Choose a payment option
Attend from 29 November and complete the capstone
coded-ai-app-developer-bootcamp-nov-2026.costs: KWD 950 (payment options listed on the bootcamp page).

general-assembly-bahrain-tamkeen-bootcam.about:
General Assembly (GA) is a global tech-education company with a campus in Bahrain, where its bootcamps are supported by Tamkeen, the Kingdom's labour fund, for Bahraini nationals. Programmes include Software Engineering, Data Analytics, Data Science, UX Design and Java Developer bootcamps, plus shorter Python, Java and Data career development programmes. Full-time bootcamps run 480 hours over 12 weeks (Sunday to Thursday, 9 am–5 pm); part-time versions run 24 weeks of evenings plus Saturdays.

The Software Engineering bootcamp, for example, teaches Python, HTML, CSS, JavaScript and APIs through five to seven hands-on projects that form a professional portfolio, with a global completion certificate. Instructors are international practitioners, and GA provides career services to help graduates into tech jobs in Bahrain.

The programmes are designed for university students, jobseekers and career changers; no specific degree or experience is required, only aptitude and motivation. New cohorts start several times a year, so students finishing school or university can plan around the next intake.
highlights: Tamkeen support for Bahraini nationals
Software engineering, data, UX and Java tracks
Full-time (12 weeks) or part-time (24 weeks) with career services
general-assembly-bahrain-tamkeen-bootcam.eligibility: Job seekers, university students and career changers in Bahrain; no technical background needed. Tamkeen support applies to Bahraini nationals (the application form asks for nationality).
how_to_apply: Choose a bootcamp on bahrain.generalassemb.ly
Fill in the 'Ready to apply?' form (programme, full- or part-time, employment status, nationality)
Attend the admissions conversation and any assessment
Confirm Tamkeen eligibility and your start date
general-assembly-bahrain-tamkeen-bootcam.costs: Tamkeen-supported for eligible Bahraini nationals; others pay GA's tuition (ask admissions for the current fee).

baymun-xix-2026.about:
BAYMUN is the student-run Model United Nations conference of the Bahrain Bayan School, founded by Bayan alumni in 2008-09 and the first MUN in Bahrain to be affiliated with The Hague International Model United Nations (THIMUN). Past editions have brought together around 600 participants from some 20 schools across the Kingdom. BAYMUN XIX takes place on 19–20 November 2026 at the school's campus in Isa Town.

The 2026 theme is 'Balancing Tomorrow's Progress': how societies can pursue smart cities, green energy and economic growth without sacrificing environment, culture, heritage and human rights. Committees include UNESCO, ECOFIN, UNEP, UNHCR, the Security Council and UN Women, two Arabic-language councils (the Arab Human Rights Committee and ALECSO), an International AI Governance Council, and creative councils such as FIA, FIFA, a Star Wars Galactic Senate, The Hunger Games and Marvel. The official site publishes a delegate guide, a chair guide and committee topic lists.

It is a well-run, affordable entry point into MUN for students in Bahrain and nearby Gulf countries, with the unusual option of debating in Arabic as well as English.
highlights: THIMUN-affiliated, student-run since 2008
15 committees including Arabic-language councils and an AI governance council
Low delegate fee and guides for first-time delegates
baymun-xix-2026.eligibility: Secondary-school students, usually registered through their school's MUN club as delegates or as chairs; individual delegates may also apply. English for most committees, Arabic for the ACHR and ALECSO councils.
how_to_apply: Read the delegate guide and committee lists on baymun.org
Click 'Apply Now' on baymun.org and register as a delegate (or through your school's MUN advisor)
Pay the delegate fee and receive your country and committee
Write your position paper and attend on 19–20 November
baymun-xix-2026.costs: Delegate fee of BHD 22 according to the registration page; travel and accommodation (for visitors from outside Bahrain) are not included.

madrasa-arabic-stem-learning-platform.about:
Madrasa is one of the Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Global Initiatives. Launched in September 2018, it offers about 5,000 video lessons in physics, chemistry, biology, mathematics and general science, covering curricula from kindergarten to grade 12, together with exercises and applications. The lessons were produced through the Translation Challenge, a large Arabic science-translation project in which hundreds of Arab volunteers translated, edited, voiced and adapted top international educational content to the curricula used in Arab countries.

In December 2020 a second phase added about 1,000 Arabic-language videos covering a full K-12 Arabic curriculum, plus cultural videos on Arabic literature and children's stories (also in the 'Madrasa Stories' app). Lessons are organised by grade and subject, with a searchable video library and 'missions' that let students earn points on a leaderboard.

The platform is free for more than 50 million Arab students wherever they are. For students in Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman it is a handy way to strengthen STEM foundations in Arabic before exams, olympiad selections or university.
highlights: About 5,000 free STEM video lessons in Arabic, K–12
Arabic language curriculum and children's stories
Exercises, missions and a student leaderboard
madrasa-arabic-stem-learning-platform.eligibility: Free for any student or teacher, anywhere. Content is in Arabic.
how_to_apply: Go to madrasa.org
Choose your grade and subject
Watch lessons and complete exercises and missions
Download the Madrasa Stories app for younger learners

rwaq-arabic-open-learning-platform.about:
Rwaq is an Arabic open-learning platform with more than 5.5 million active learners and over 21,000 learning components. Its catalogue spans economics, management and marketing; computer science and digital skills; literature and the Arabic language; creativity and innovation; and Islamic studies. Many courses are free and taught by university professors and practitioners, for example Business Fundamentals, Microsoft Excel, Computational Thinking, Generative AI for Everyone (Copilot and ChatGPT), Marketing Psychology, KPIs and OKRs, and Teaching Arabic to Non-Native Speakers.

Alongside free courses, Rwaq offers career-track programmes (data analyst, software engineer, UX designer, project manager, AI engineer, digital marketer, cybersecurity specialist) and preparation for professional certificates from Google, IBM, Microsoft, Meta and CompTIA, some of which are paid. It also runs a free Comprehensive Entrepreneurship Licence (ILFEN) track with live sessions, and a career-interest assessment.

For school leavers and university students in Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman and the wider Arab world, Rwaq is a flexible way to learn job-ready and academic skills in Arabic and add certificates to a CV.
highlights: Many free courses in Arabic from university lecturers
Career tracks and professional-certificate prep
More than 5.5 million learners
rwaq-arabic-open-learning-platform.eligibility: Anyone who can study in Arabic. Free account registration.
how_to_apply: Go to rwaq.org and create a free account
Browse categories or search for a course
Enrol in a free course (marked 'مجاني') and study at your pace
Complete assessments to earn a certificate where offered
rwaq-arabic-open-learning-platform.costs: Many courses free; some programmes and certificate preparation are paid (price shown on each page).

hmc-middle-east-2027.about:
Harvard Model Congress Middle East (HMCME) is the regional edition of Harvard Model Congress, the largest congressional simulation in the world, organised entirely by Harvard College undergraduates. The fourteenth annual session takes place from 14 to 16 January 2027 at Qatar Foundation's Academic Bridge Program in Education City, Doha, its second year in partnership with Qatar Foundation, next to Georgetown and Northwestern's Qatar campuses. The 2027 theme is "Progress Under Pressure".

Delegates spend most of the conference in committee sessions built on briefings written by Harvard students. They take the roles of US representatives and senators, Qatari Shura Council members, agency officials and UN country delegates, negotiate compromises and draft legislation. There is a novice committee (House Judiciary) for first-timers, an experienced committee (Senate Homeland Security) and a women-only Arab League committee. Workshops and leadership seminars run alongside the committees.

Any high school student (usually 14–18) can attend, either with a school delegation led by a faculty advisor or as an independent delegate. Need-based financial-aid grants reduce the delegate fee for students who could not otherwise attend (they do not cover travel or hotels). It is one of the few Harvard-run conferences held in the Gulf, which makes it an affordable way for students in Qatar and the region to get Harvard-style debate training without flying to Boston.
highlights: Committees chaired and written by Harvard undergraduates
Novice, experienced and women-only (Arab League) committees
Need-based financial aid for the delegate fee
hmc-middle-east-2027.eligibility: High school students of any nationality, typically aged 14–18. Each delegation needs a faculty advisor (teacher or parent); individual delegates may register on their own. No limit on delegation size.

Register your school or yourself on the HMCME 2027 registration portal and pay the delegate (and school) fee

Return the code-of-conduct forms by 5 January 2027 and complete your committee pre-conference assignment
Attend the conference at the Academic Bridge Program, Education City, 14–16 January 2027
hmc-middle-east-2027.costs: Per-delegate fee (plus a school fee where applicable) paid at registration; amounts are shown in the registration portal. Payments are non-refundable. Need-based grants available; travel and accommodation are not covered.

qatardebate-qatar-schools-debate-league-.about:
The Qatar Schools Debate League (QSDL) is the main competitive debate circuit for school students in Qatar, run by the QatarDebate Center, a Qatar Foundation member founded in 2008. Throughout the academic year QatarDebate holds a series of league rounds and national championships for preparatory and secondary students, with separate tournaments for girls and boys and for each school stage, in Arabic and English.

Teams debate current affairs, ethics, technology and policy motions in formats such as World Schools style. Strong QSDL debaters are invited to QatarDebate's Masterclass training and are scouted for the national team that represents Qatar at the World Schools Debating Championships. Participation is organised through schools, so there is no individual entry fee.

It is the best entry point into debating in Qatar: it builds public speaking, research and critical thinking, gives students a recognised competitive record for university applications, and connects them to QatarDebate's international Arabic championships.
highlights: Arabic and English leagues for preparatory and secondary stages
Pathway to the Qatar national team and QatarDebate Masterclass
Free for students; organised through schools
qatardebate-qatar-schools-debate-league-.eligibility: Students at preparatory and secondary schools in Qatar (public, private and international), entered by their school.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's debate coordinator to register a team for the QSDL
If your school has no debate club, email qdep@qf.org.qa to request a workshop or registration
Attend QatarDebate training workshops before league rounds
Compete in league rounds and qualify for the national championship
qatardebate-qatar-schools-debate-league-.costs: No individual fee for league participation; schools organise transport. Optional Debate Academy training costs QAR 500 per semester.

qatardebate-qatar-universities-debate-le.about:
The Qatar Universities Debate League (QUDL) brings together debate teams from every university in Qatar, including Qatar University, HBKU, UDST and the Education City branch campuses. QatarDebate runs a series of league tournaments through the academic year, in Arabic and English and in formats such as British Parliamentary, followed by a national championship.

The league is the main route to selection for the international university championships that QatarDebate hosts in Doha, such as the International Universities Debating Championship, which brings hundreds of Arabic-speaking debaters from dozens of countries. Students also gain judging experience and access to QatarDebate coaching.

For university students it is a free way to build argumentation, research and public-speaking skills, meet students across Qatar's universities and represent their institution.
highlights: Open to every university in Qatar
Arabic and English tournaments plus a national championship
Route to QatarDebate's international university championships
qatardebate-qatar-universities-debate-le.eligibility: Undergraduate and graduate students enrolled at universities in Qatar, via their university debate club.
how_to_apply: Join your university's debate club
If your university has no club, email qdep@qf.org.qa
Attend QatarDebate training sessions
Compete in league rounds during the academic year
qatardebate-qatar-universities-debate-le.costs: No participation fee for league rounds through member university clubs.

qatardebate-qatar-connects-2026-27.about:
Qatar Connects is a dialogue series by the QatarDebate Center that brings together young people from different backgrounds in Qatar with field experts to talk about the society they live in. Each episode is a one-hour moderated conversation at Education City, with audience questions and networking.

Episode 5 (Tuesday 3 November 2026, 5:30 pm) explores the Qatari house as the product of families, hospitality customs, municipal rules, climate adaptation and the work of contractors and artisans. Earlier episodes asked whether Qatar can build homegrown consulting firms at global standards.

Sessions are free and open to the public with registration. They suit high school and university students who want to practise listening to and questioning experts, and to understand Qatar's development beyond textbooks.
highlights: Free, open to the public with registration
Experts and young Qataris in moderated conversation
Good introduction to QatarDebate's wider programmes
qatardebate-qatar-connects-2026-27.eligibility: Open to the public; aimed at youth and students living in Qatar. Sessions may be in Arabic.
how_to_apply: Open the Qatar Connects event page on qatardebate.org
Register on the attendee form linked from the page
Attend the session at Education City

wcmq-qatar-medical-explorer-program-summ.about:
The Qatar Medical Explorer Program (QMEP) is Weill Cornell Medicine-Qatar's main enrichment programme for school students who are curious about becoming doctors. The summer edition is a two-week on-campus experience in Education City, led by WCM-Q pre-medical and medical faculty and recent graduates.

Participants rotate through clinical skills workshops, problem-based learning cases like those used in medical school, career counselling, personal-development sessions, college presentations, personal-statement writing and admissions-style practice interviews. A winter edition (by school nomination only) adds hands-on research experience.

WCM-Q is the only medical school in Qatar to award the Cornell MD, and QMEP is the most direct way for a high school student to see its six-year medical programme from the inside, meet faculty and decide whether medicine is the right path before applying.
highlights: Clinical-skills and problem-based learning workshops
Practice interviews and personal-statement coaching for medical school
Taught by WCM-Q faculty in Education City

Complete the online application with your school transcript
Attend the two-week programme in summer 2027 if selected
wcmq-qatar-medical-explorer-program-summ.costs: WCM-Q outreach programmes have no published fee; confirm when the call opens.

wcmq-doctors-of-the-future-conference-20.about:
The Doctors of the Future Conference is Weill Cornell Medicine-Qatar's yearly event for high school students who are thinking about a career in medicine or health sciences. The 2027 edition is in April at WCM-Q in Education City, Doha. It combines talks and panel discussions with doctors, WCM-Q students and faculty, research poster presentations by school teams, and Medicine Unlimited, a community fair where families explore healthcare careers through hands-on stations.

School teams that qualified through the High School Science Competition (themes based on the UN Sustainable Development Goals) present their research and the top three teams receive awards. Other students attend as audience members to learn how to prepare for medical school, what the six-year Cornell MD involves and which subjects to take.

It is a free, low-pressure way for grades 9–12 students and their parents to meet WCM-Q admissions staff, current medical students and practising clinicians in one day.
highlights: Panels with doctors, faculty and medical students
High school research posters and awards
Medicine Unlimited careers fair for families
wcmq-doctors-of-the-future-conference-20.eligibility: High school students (grades 9–12) and their families; mainly students in Qatar. Presenting at the conference requires having qualified through the science competition.
how_to_apply: Watch the conference page for registration opening in early December 2026
Register to attend (individually or with your school)
Attend the conference at WCM-Q, Education City, in April 2027

wise-edtech-accelerator-2026-27.about:
The WISE EdTech Accelerator is the startup programme of WISE, the World Innovation Summit for Education, an initiative of Qatar Foundation. Each cycle selects four to six early-stage edtech ventures (seed to pre-series A) from a global applicant pool; the acceptance rate is about 5 percent. There are two tracks: a Local Track for startups ready to enter the Qatari education market, run with QSTP, QRDI and other local partners, and an International Track for startups scaling anywhere in the world.

Selected teams start in January 2027 and receive one-to-one coaching, masterclasses with industry experts on product, marketing, sales and fundraising, more than 100 hours of mentoring, in-person bootcamps at major education conferences such as Web Summit Qatar and London EdTech Week, and promotion across WISE platforms. The cohort presents at the WISE 13 Summit in Doha in late 2027, in front of more than 4,000 education leaders from 100 countries. There is no programme fee.

Applications for 2026–2027 opened on 28 September 2026 and close on 31 October 2026. Teams with co-founders covering product, marketing and sales are preferred. Shortlisted startups are interviewed in November–December and the cohort is announced in December 2026 or early January 2027. For student founders already building an edtech product with traction, it is one of the most visible education accelerators in the Middle East.
highlights: Local (Qatar) and International tracks
Coaching, masterclasses and investor network; no programme fee
Pitch at the WISE Summit in Doha to 4,000+ attendees
wise-edtech-accelerator-2026-27.eligibility: Early-stage education-technology startups (seed to pre-series A) from any country, with a working product. Co-founding teams preferred. Application in English.
how_to_apply: Read the selection criteria on the WISE EdTech Accelerator page
Choose the Local (Qatar) or International track
Complete the online application in English on wise-qatar.awardsplatform.com before 31 October 2026
If shortlisted, attend an interview in November–December 2026
Join the programme in January 2027 if selected
wise-edtech-accelerator-2026-27.costs: No fee to apply or participate. Travel to some in-person events may be supported; check with WISE.

qstp-internship-program-2027.about:
The QSTP Internship Program places senior university students and recent graduates with carefully matched startups and teams at Qatar Science & Technology Park, Qatar Foundation's technology hub in Education City. Interns work on live projects in product development, engineering, data, marketing and business strategy, mentored by founders and industry professionals.

Each cycle lasts 12 weeks and runs three times a year: Winter (29 January – 21 April), Summer (14 June – 3 September) and Fall (1 October – 24 December). Interns choose part-time (20 hours a week, compatible with classes) or full-time (40 hours a week). The programme also feeds into QSTP's hackathons, incubation programme and fellowship.

It is one of the few structured ways for students in Qatar to gain real startup experience, build a CV with deep-tech companies and join Qatar's innovation network before graduating.
highlights: Matched placements with QSTP startups
Part-time option that fits around classes
Three cycles a year: Winter, Summer, Fall
qstp-internship-program-2027.eligibility: Final-year students or graduates of the past two years, enrolled at (or graduated from) a university in Qatar, with relevant skills or interest in technology, innovation or entrepreneurship.

qstp-internship-program-2027.costs: Free to apply. Compensation, if any, is not stated on the page.

qstp-ride-and-pitch-2027.about:
Ride and Pitch is QSTP's pitching programme for student entrepreneurs. Over three days, participants receive mentorship and pitch-development sessions from experienced coaches (day 1), one-to-one feedback from industry experts and deck refinement (day 2), and then deliver their final pitch aboard the moving Education City tram in front of judges, investors and a live audience (day 3).

It is designed for students who have an innovative startup idea or are in the early stages of building one. Winning teams receive prizes and visibility in Qatar's startup community, and strong teams are often directed to QSTP's incubation programme and hackathons.

The programme runs twice a year. It is free, in person, and a low-risk way to practise pitching under pressure and get honest feedback from people who fund startups.
highlights: Pitch to investors on the Education City tram
Two days of coaching and one-to-one expert feedback
Prizes and links to QSTP incubation
qstp-ride-and-pitch-2027.eligibility: Students currently enrolled at universities in Qatar with an innovative startup idea or early-stage startup, comfortable presenting in public and able to attend all three days.
how_to_apply: Submit the online register-your-interest/application form on the QSTP page
If shortlisted, attend the orientation session
Complete two days of mentorship and coaching
Pitch live aboard the Education City tram

qstp-summer-bootcamp-2027.about:
QSTP's Summer Bootcamp is an intensive four-week programme that gives students and early professionals direct access to leaders in Qatar's technology, business and innovation sectors. Interactive workshops run on Mondays, Tuesdays and Wednesdays, with site visits and tours on Thursdays.

Participants work through real startup and business case studies, expert talks and hands-on challenges, then form teams for a closing hackathon. In 2026 this was the four-day QSTP x Young Entrepreneurs Club Bootcamp Hackathon (20–23 August), where 100 applicants built deep-tech startup ideas and minimum viable products and pitched to judges, with partners including Qatar University, the Ministry of Sports and Youth and Microsoft Qatar.

It suits anyone in Qatar who is considering launching a venture or joining a startup and wants a practical summer that builds networks across the ecosystem.
highlights: Workshops with Qatar's top tech and innovation leaders
Weekly site visits to companies
Ends in a deep-tech startup hackathon
qstp-summer-bootcamp-2027.eligibility: Students and young professionals in Qatar interested in innovation, technology and entrepreneurship.
how_to_apply: Submit the register-your-interest form on the QSTP Summer Bootcamp page
Watch for the 2027 call (expected in late spring)
Attend the four-week bootcamp and join a hackathon team

eaa-rota-youth-volunteer-programme.about:
Education Above All (EAA) is a global foundation established in Doha in 2012 by Her Highness Sheikha Moza bint Nasser to give out-of-school children and young people access to quality education. Its youth programme, ROTA (Reach Out To All, formerly Reach Out To Asia), runs the foundation's volunteer network.

Volunteers support EAA's own events, partner-led events and ongoing commitments in Qatar, such as International Youth Day activations, community walks like "Let's Move for Education" and awareness campaigns. Each role has a description stating its purpose, duties, timeframe and selection criteria; recruitment is merit-based and inclusive.

Volunteering with EAA is a straightforward way for school and university students in Qatar to log community-service hours with a respected international foundation, build event and communication skills and learn how global education work is done.
highlights: Open from age 15
Events and ongoing roles with a global education foundation
Simple online registration in English or Arabic

Complete the online volunteer registration form (personal, contact, emergency and experience details)
Wait to be contacted when a role matches your profile
Attend the briefing for your assigned event or project

qnl-volunteer-programme.about:
Qatar National Library (QNL), a Qatar Foundation member in Education City, is one of the largest and most visited libraries in the Middle East, with a heritage collection, children's and young adults' libraries and a busy year-round events programme. Its volunteer scheme lets students and recent graduates contribute to library life.

Applicants submit an online form with their school or university, field of study, languages, skills, the period they are available and a CV. QNL then matches volunteers to needs such as supporting public events, children's and teen activities, exhibitions and visitor services.

For school and university students it is a flexible way to gain verified volunteer experience in a world-class cultural institution, practise customer service and event work, and meet people across Qatar's education and research community.
highlights: Choose your own dates and duration
Volunteer at one of the region's flagship libraries
Good fit for community-service hours

Fill in personal, education and skills details and the dates you are available
Upload your CV (PDF/DOC, up to 2 MB) and submit
Wait for QNL to contact you with a placement

qnl-murshidi-mentorship-program.about:
Murshidi ("my guide") is Qatar National Library's mentoring programme. It pairs students with volunteer mentors drawn from Education City universities, their alumni and other institutions in Qatar for one-to-one guidance on choosing and applying to universities, finding scholarships, planning a career and succeeding in academic and professional settings.

Sessions take place every Saturday from 10:00 to 13:00 at the library's Main Plaza or online. Students fill in a registration form describing what they need help with and choose three or four preferred mentors from the published mentor list; QNL staff then assign a mentor based on availability.

It is especially useful for high school students preparing applications (personal statements, choosing majors, scholarship options) and for first-year university students or recent graduates thinking about their next step, and it costs nothing.
highlights: Free one-to-one mentoring every Saturday
Mentors from Education City universities and alumni
In person at QNL or online

Complete the Murshidi registration form and state the topics you need help with
Select three or four preferred mentors
Attend your assigned Saturday session at QNL or online

cmuq-alice-programming-competition-2027.about:
Alice Middle East is a version of Carnegie Mellon's Alice 3D programming environment adapted for the region and used, in partnership with Qatar's Ministry of Education and Higher Education, to teach computational thinking to thousands of students every year. The Alice Programming Competition is the annual national contest built on it, hosted by CMU-Q with the Hamad Bin Jassim Center for Computer Science Education.

Teams of middle and high school students create interactive stories and games that tackle real-world themes such as sustainability, food security, inclusive education, cultural heritage and renewable energy. Expert judges evaluate creativity, technical execution and thematic impact, and the showcase and final take place at CMU-Q in Education City.

The competition is an accessible first step into programming and game design: no prior coding experience beyond Alice is needed, and finalists meet CMU-Q computer science faculty and students.
highlights: Build 3D games and animations on real-world themes
Judged by experts at CMU-Q
Beginner-friendly entry to programming

Watch the CMU-Q competition page for 2027 registration details
Form a team, build your project on the announced theme and submit it
Present at the showcase in Education City if selected as a finalist

cmuq-lifelines-hackathon-2027.about:
LifeLines is a humanitarian innovation initiative created by CMU-Q undergraduates who wanted to use their skills to reduce the impact of global crises. Its annual hackathon, hosted by CMU-Q with the Hamad Bin Jassim Center for Computer Science Education, brings together students, educators and professionals around the idea of "software that saves lives".

The event combines brainstorming sessions, workshops on design thinking and rapid prototyping, and hands-on guidance from industry, academic and NGO mentors. Teams then build a working prototype addressing a humanitarian challenge, such as crisis communication, refugee services or health access, and pitch it to expert judges.

Because it welcomes high school students alongside university students and developers, it is one of the best first hackathons in Qatar for a school student who codes and cares about social impact.
highlights: Open to high school and university students
Design-thinking and prototyping workshops
Mentors from industry, academia and NGOs

cmuq-pi-day-mathematics-competition-2027.about:
The Pi Day Mathematics Competition celebrates Pi Day (3/14) by inviting high school students in Qatar to explore the fun side of mathematics. The 2027 edition takes place on 3 April 2027 in the CMU-Q building in Education City.

Each school may register one team of exactly four students from the same school plus one faculty or staff advisor. Teams solve problems in a preliminary round; the top four teams advance to a final round. Problems are in English with Arabic translations available, and the content follows the Ministry of Education and Higher Education curriculum standards for grades 9 to 11, so no olympiad-level preparation is required.

It is a friendly but competitive way for strong maths students to represent their school, experience a university campus and meet CMU-Q mathematics faculty.
highlights: One team of four per school
English problems with Arabic translations
Content based on grades 9–11 curriculum

Form a team of four from your school with one advisor
Compete in the preliminary round on 3 April 2027; top four teams go to the final

qf-math-circle-2026-27.about:
QF Math Circle is a weekly after-school programme for high school students who love mathematics. Founded in 2023 by mathematics faculty from Education City universities (CMU-Q, Hamad Bin Khalifa University, Texas A&M at Qatar, VCUarts Qatar and Weill Cornell Medicine-Qatar) with input from Qatar Foundation school teachers, it introduces topics students rarely meet in school.

Sessions run on Mondays during the academic year at different Education City campuses. The November 2026 schedule includes combinatorics (Dr Samir Belhaouari), number theory (Dr Hasan Demirkoparan) and a session at WCM-Q. Past topics include tournament design, infinite sets, the distribution of primes, Monte-Carlo methods, graph theory, fractals and modular arithmetic, taught interactively.

Students in grades 10 and 11 are accepted according to their interest and curiosity rather than grades alone. It is excellent preparation for maths olympiads, university-level thinking and STEM applications, and it is free.
highlights: Taught by professors from five Education City universities
Topics beyond the school curriculum
Free, weekly, after school

Attend the Monday sessions listed on the CMU-Q page

cmuq-summer-college-preview-program-2027.about:
The Summer College Preview Program (SCPP) gives ambitious high school students in Qatar a taste of studying at an elite university. For three weeks in the CMU-Q building in Education City, participants follow a track in one of CMU-Q's four disciplines: biological sciences, business administration, computer science or information systems.

Alongside academic classes, students learn about career paths, work in teams, and attend workshops on goal setting, time management and preparing a competitive university application. Historically almost one in five CMU-Q first-year students had completed SCPP, so it is also a strong signal of interest for anyone considering Carnegie Mellon.

The application asks for two 300–500-word essays (why you are applying and which universities and majors interest you), school transcripts and any test scores (TOEFL, IELTS, PSAT, SAT, ACT). Applications are reviewed in order of submission, so applying early in 2027 matters.
highlights: Choose biology, business, computer science or information systems
University application workshops
Pathway many CMU-Q students took

Pay the USD 750 fee if admitted

cmuq-experience-cmuq-november-2026.about:
Experience CMU-Q is a one-day introduction to the disciplines taught at Carnegie Mellon University in Qatar. Each participant chooses one programme for the day (biological sciences, business administration, computer science or information systems) and spends it on hands-on activities designed by CMU-Q faculty, staff and current students.

Because the sessions are taught by the people who run the degrees, it is an excellent chance to ask honest questions about university life, workload, admissions and careers. Some students attend more than once to compare majors.

All high school students in Qatar can apply; places are limited and first-time attendees get priority. The next workshop is on Saturday 21 November 2026 in the CMU-Q building, Education City.

Taught by faculty and current students
Free; priority for first-time attendees

cmuq-future-finance-leaders-2026.about:
Future Finance Leaders is a hands-on workshop by CMU-Q's Business Administration programme for high school students who want early financial capability. Faculty, staff and students cover personal finance foundations, how investments and markets work, wealth creation and how data and artificial intelligence are integrated into modern finance.

The 2026 workshops take place on 5 November and 19 November at CMU-Q in Education City. Teachers are invited too, to bring financial literacy into their classrooms. Students who complete the workshop receive a certificate.

It is a good fit for students considering business, economics or finance degrees and a useful line on a university application, at no cost.
highlights: Personal finance, investing and AI in finance

nuq-pre-college-programs-2026-27.about:
Northwestern University in Qatar (NU-Q), the Education City branch of Northwestern's renowned journalism and communication schools, offers pre-college courses for high school students during the fall, spring and summer semesters, both on campus and online. Each course is taught by an NU-Q professor and ends with a finished piece of work that strengthens a university application portfolio.

The 2026–27 line-up includes The Art of the Podcast (virtual, audio documentaries and podcast formats), Storytelling (in person), Story to Screen (a hands-on filmmaking bootcamp in which students write a short script and shoot a scene, covering camera, sound, directing, acting and basic editing) and Digital Journalism (reporting a publication-ready online news video package, with fact-checking and verification). Virtual courses run in the late afternoon Qatar time via Zoom; equipment is mostly a computer, headphones and a smartphone.

The programme is ideal for students considering journalism, film, communication or media degrees, at NU-Q or elsewhere, who want an authentic university-level project and a recommendation-ready experience with faculty.
highlights: Taught by Northwestern Qatar faculty
Podcasting, filmmaking, storytelling and journalism tracks
Finished project for your application portfolio
