doha-debates-ambassador-program-2027.about:
Doha Debates is Qatar Foundation's global media platform for live debates and solutions-focused conversations. Its Ambassador Program is a virtual convening of young leaders from across the globe who want to change how public discourse happens, inspired by the majlis, the traditional Gulf space for open discussion.

Over 12 weeks, ambassadors build intercultural communication, systems-thinking and debate skills through expert-led training, mentored collaboration in small learning circles and personal storytelling. They practise facilitating conversations on complex global issues, understanding other people's motivations, and then host their own community discussions at home, school or work.

Ambassadors join an international peer network, gain access to Doha Debates facilitators and mentors, and are invited to engage with Doha Debates staff and events afterwards. It suits university students and young professionals interested in dialogue, journalism, diplomacy or community leadership who want a global network without travelling.
highlights: Free and fully virtual
Training in facilitation, debate and systems thinking
Global peer network and Doha Debates mentors
doha-debates-ambassador-program-2027.eligibility: Young leaders from anywhere in the world; Doha Debates does not publish a strict age range (past cohorts were mostly students and young professionals). English required.
how_to_apply: Follow Doha Debates' website and social media for the 2027 application announcement
Submit the online application when it opens
Join the 12-week virtual programme if selected

qatar-sustainability-week-2026.about:
Qatar Sustainability Week (QSW) is an annual national campaign led by Earthna Center for a Sustainable Future, a Qatar Foundation member, with the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change, and with the Ministry of Education as a strategic partner. Since 2016 it has drawn about one million participants, 3,400 events and 2,000 partner organisations.

During the week, anyone can register an event, initiative or activity, such as a school clean-up, recycling drive, awareness talk, sustainable food fair, tree planting, workshop or sports activity, under categories including Awareness, Schools and Kids, Seminars and Conferences and Initiatives. Registered activities appear on the official QSW calendar, and the public can join hundreds of free events across Qatar. Qatar Museums' Teen Hub is among the partners.

For students it is a simple way to lead a visible environmental project, get it recognised on a national platform and gain community-service and leadership experience; for others it is a week of free talks and activities.
highlights: Register your own school or club green event
Hundreds of free activities across Qatar
Run by Qatar Foundation's Earthna with two ministries
qatar-sustainability-week-2026.eligibility: Open to everyone in Qatar: schools, universities, student clubs, NGOs, companies and individuals.
how_to_apply: Plan a sustainability activity with your school, club or friends
Register it via 'Register your Event / Initiative / Activity' on the QSW website
Run the activity between 31 October and 7 November 2026
Or browse the QSW calendar and join existing events
qatar-sustainability-week-2026.costs: Free to register and to attend most events.

dfi-ajyal-film-club-festival-edition-202.about:
The Ajyal Film Club is the Doha Film Institute's year-round initiative that uses cinema to build curiosity, empathy and self-expression in young people. Its Festival Edition gathers children and young teens for three days of carefully selected films, guided discussions and creative activities during DFI's festival season at Katara Cultural Village.

There are two age streams: Mohaq (ages 8–11) on 20–22 November 2026 and Hilal (ages 12–15) on 23–25 November 2026. Participants watch films from around the world, talk about them with facilitators and peers, and take part in hands-on activities that show film as a way to start conversations and explore ideas.

It is an accessible first step into DFI's youth programmes, which later include the Ajyal juries for older teens, and it introduces young viewers to film criticism and storytelling in a festival setting.
highlights: Festival-season screenings at Katara
Separate streams for ages 8–11 and 12–15
Guided discussions and creative workshops
dfi-ajyal-film-club-festival-edition-202.eligibility: Children and young teens aged 8–15 (Mohaq 8–11, Hilal 12–15). Under-18s need parent or guardian consent. Mainly for families living in Qatar.
how_to_apply: Open the Ajyal Film Club: Festival Edition page on dohafilm.com
Click Register Now and choose the right age stream
Complete the form with parental consent and pay the QR 150 fee before 8 November 2026
Attend all three days at Katara Cultural Village

qatar-museums-volunteer-programme.about:
Qatar Museums (QM) runs the country's major cultural institutions, including the Museum of Islamic Art, the National Museum of Qatar, Mathaf: Arab Museum of Modern Art, the 3-2-1 Qatar Olympic and Sports Museum and Fire Station, as well as large public art and festival programmes. Its Volunteer Programme invites the public to become part of this cultural community.

Volunteers support events, exhibitions, training programmes and guided tours, and get behind-the-scenes opportunities, learning about Qatar's history, culture and heritage while developing communication and event skills. Volunteers must be at least 12 years old; younger children can join only with a registered family member or guardian.

Because the minimum age is low and roles change with QM's busy calendar of exhibitions and festivals, it is one of the most accessible ways for middle and high school students in Qatar to gain recognised volunteer experience in the arts and culture sector.
highlights: Open from age 12
Exhibitions, festivals and guided tours at Qatar's major museums
Behind-the-scenes learning about heritage and the arts
qatar-museums-volunteer-programme.eligibility: Anyone aged 12 or over (under-12s only with a registered guardian). Residency requirements are not stated; roles are in Qatar.
how_to_apply: Go to the QM volunteer portal (volunteers.qm.org.qa) and click Register to Volunteer
Create your profile and choose areas of interest
Sign up for opportunities as they are posted
Email volunteers@qm.org.qa with questions

hbku-qbri-summer-research-program-2027.about:
The Summer Research Program (SRP) of the Qatar Biomedical Research Institute (QBRI) at Hamad Bin Khalifa University is an annual initiative that has run for ten editions. For seven weeks, undergraduate students join faculty-led research projects and use QBRI's laboratories and core facilities in Education City.

Projects align with QBRI's three centres: the Diabetes Research Center, the Translational Oncology Research Center and the Neurological Disorders Research Center. Alongside lab work, participants attend seminars and workshops on research careers, scientific communication and lab skills, and present their results at the end of the programme.

For students aiming at medical school, a PhD or biotech careers, it offers rare hands-on biomedical research experience in Qatar and a mentor who can write a strong reference letter.
highlights: Faculty-mentored lab research in diabetes, cancer or neuroscience
Career and research-skills seminars
Annual, open to students from institutions across Qatar
hbku-qbri-summer-research-program-2027.eligibility: Undergraduate students enrolled in a biological or medical-related science programme at an institution in Qatar, with a minimum GPA of 3.0.
how_to_apply: Watch HBKU's QBRI news and events pages for the 2027 call (expected early 2027)
Prepare your transcript and a statement of research interest
Submit the online application on the HBKU event page before the deadline
Start the seven-week programme in late May or June if selected

hbku-qcri-summer-internship-2027.about:
Qatar Computing Research Institute (QCRI), part of Hamad Bin Khalifa University, is Qatar's national computing research institute, known for Arabic natural-language processing, the AI tools behind crisis informatics, cybersecurity and data science. Each summer it hosts undergraduate and graduate interns on real research projects.

In 2026 the programme ran in two eight-week cohorts (one for Education City and other institutions, one for Qatar University students), weekdays 08:30–15:30 in Education City, with a break for Eid al-Adha. Applicants read the published project descriptions and choose two research areas: Arabic Language Technologies, Cybersecurity, Data Analytics, Social Computing or Software Engineering.

Interns work alongside QCRI scientists, often contributing to papers and open-source tools, which makes the programme a strong stepping stone to graduate school or AI and data careers.
highlights: Real research projects with QCRI scientists
Arabic NLP, cybersecurity, data analytics and more
Separate cohorts for Education City and Qatar University students
hbku-qcri-summer-internship-2027.eligibility: Undergraduate and graduate students at universities in Qatar (Education City universities, Qatar University and other institutions).
how_to_apply: Watch the HBKU/QCRI events page for the 2027 internship announcement (expected around March)
Read the project descriptions and pick two research areas
Submit the online application form during the application window
Interview and start in May if selected

qatar-award-scientific-excellence-2027.about:
The Qatar Award for Scientific Excellence was established by the Ministry of Education and Higher Education in the 2006–2007 school year, building on the older Science Day tradition, to celebrate outstanding achievers and promote a culture of excellence in line with Qatar National Vision 2030.

The 2027 cycle has nine categories: Outstanding Student at the primary, preparatory and secondary certificate levels; bachelor's degree holders; master's degree holders; doctorate holders; scientific research; outstanding teacher; and outstanding school. Each category has its own indicative guide and nomination form setting out the evidence required (grades, achievements, research, community contribution). Electronic submissions opened on 1 October 2026 and close on 31 October 2026; winners are announced on 4 February 2027 and honoured at a ceremony on 18 April 2027 under the patronage of His Highness the Amir.

For high-achieving Qatari students it is the most prestigious national recognition available, carries a ministry-approved prize, and is a strong distinction for scholarship and university applications.
highlights: Categories from primary school to PhD
Awarded under the patronage of the Amir
Strong distinction for scholarship applications
qatar-award-scientific-excellence-2027.eligibility: Outstanding Qatari students and graduates (the award honours achievers from Qatar); each category has its own criteria in the official guide. Teachers and schools have separate categories.
how_to_apply: Download the indicative guide and nomination form for your category from the award site
Create an account or log in on educompetitions.edu.gov.qa
Upload your documents and submit through 'Apply Now' before 31 October 2026
Wait for the results announcement on 4 February 2027
qatar-award-scientific-excellence-2027.costs: Free. Prize values are approved by the Ministry for each category.

qatar-scientific-club-innovation-project.about:
The Qatar Scientific Club, affiliated with the Ministry of Sports and Youth, is Qatar's main community space for young inventors, makers and science enthusiasts. Besides camps such as the Science and Technology Pioneers summer camp and the Young Inventors programme, it runs a year-round project registration service for people with an invention idea.

Registered inventors receive modelling and prototyping services to turn their idea into a working prototype, guidance on registering intellectual property rights (which remain with the inventor), confidentiality for the idea, and the chance to have the project presented at local and international exhibitions and in the media under their name. Fields include mechanics, making and innovation, electronics, software and renewable energy. Inventors commit to working on the project regularly and to joining exhibitions the club enters.

For school and university students with a serious invention, it offers lab access and expert help that are hard to find elsewhere, and a route to innovation fairs where Qatari projects regularly win awards.
highlights: Prototyping help and IP guidance
Projects shown at local and international exhibitions
Fields from electronics to renewable energy
qatar-scientific-club-innovation-project.eligibility: Young people in Qatar with an invention idea (the club's youth programmes target ages 15–35). Membership registration asks for a valid Qatari ID, so priority is likely for Qatari nationals; confirm with the club.
how_to_apply: Optionally register as a club member on qsc.org.qa/register
Fill in the project registration form with your project name, field, description and drawing
Add estimated cost, duration and required materials and submit
Meet the club team to plan prototyping

vcuarts-qatar-portfolio-development-clas.about:
VCUarts Qatar, the Education City campus of Virginia Commonwealth University's top-ranked School of the Arts, runs a Portfolio Development Program of non-credit classes taught by its alumni for high school students who want to study art, design or architecture. Class E of fall 2026 is fully online, so students anywhere can join.

Over eight live sessions (Sundays and Tuesdays, 5:00–8:00 pm Qatar time, 22 November to 15 December 2026) students work through creative direction and idea generation, experimentation with materials and visual language, research and concept development, technical making, observational drawing, building a cohesive body of work, and final selection and presentation. They keep a sketchbook, produce drawing studies, a three-dimensional project and a digital or time-based experiment, and learn to photograph and upload their work. Each student gets individual portfolio feedback.

The instructor is Salma Awad, a VCUarts Qatar painting and printmaking graduate and former admissions counsellor, so the course is closely aligned with what art schools look for. Materials are mostly household items.
highlights: Taught by a VCUarts Qatar alumna and former admissions counsellor
Individual portfolio review
Fully online with household materials
vcuarts-qatar-portfolio-development-clas.eligibility: High school students preparing art, design or architecture portfolios. Open online; English instruction.
how_to_apply: Read the class page on qatar.vcu.edu
Register through the online form linked on the page
Pay the QAR 1,600 fee
Join the first live session on 22 November 2026
vcuarts-qatar-portfolio-development-clas.costs: QAR 1,600 for 8 sessions. Students need a computer or tablet with camera and basic art materials.

qnl-innovation-stations-workshops-2026.about:
Qatar National Library's Innovation Stations are makerspaces with professional equipment for audio and video production, photography, design and digital fabrication that members can use for free. The "Explore the Innovation Stations" workshop series teaches young people how to use them.

In November 2026 the teen and young-adult programme includes Digital Content Creation (Saturday 7 November, 11:00–13:00), a hands-on introduction to Canva for visuals, CapCut for short videos and DaVinci Resolve for basic professional editing, and Photography & Videography (Saturday 14 November, 11:00–13:00), on what makes a strong photo or video with a professional camera or a smartphone. Sessions are in English and registration is per session.

The workshops are a free way to build portfolio-ready media skills and to unlock independent use of the library's studios afterwards.
highlights: Free, hands-on, in English
Canva, CapCut, DaVinci Resolve, camera skills
Opens access to QNL's media studios
qnl-innovation-stations-workshops-2026.eligibility: Teens and young adults; QNL membership (free for Qatar residents) is useful for later studio use.
how_to_apply: Open the QNL Young Adults events page
Pick a session and register on the QNL events portal
Attend at Qatar National Library, Education City

qnl-literacy-essentials-research-worksho.about:
LiteracyEssentials@QNL is Qatar National Library's series of short workshops on information, digital and research literacy, run by QNL librarians and partners such as the National Cyber Security Agency.

The November 2026 sessions are: Your Privacy First, on essentials of personal data protection (3 November, 12:00–13:00); Exploring the Publishing Journey and Enhancing Research Visibility, on journal selection and manuscript submission (19 November, 17:00–18:30); Fundamentals of Research Integrity and Publishing Ethics in the Era of AI, on authorship, acceptable AI use and post-publication notices (24 November, 11:00–12:00); and Increasing the Real-World Impact of Your Research, on using social media to reach wider audiences (25 November, 17:00–19:00). All are in English.

They are particularly useful for undergraduates writing a thesis or first paper, students in research programmes such as UREP, and anyone who wants to publish responsibly.
highlights: Free, short and practical
Publishing, research ethics and AI use
Run by QNL librarians and national partners
qnl-literacy-essentials-research-worksho.eligibility: Open to the public; aimed at university students, graduate students and early-career researchers.
how_to_apply: Open the QNL events page
Choose a LiteracyEssentials@QNL session and register on the QNL events portal
Attend at the library (check the listing for online options)

kaust-visiting-student-research-program.about:
The Visiting Student Research Program (VSRP) lets undergraduate and master's students spend two to six months doing real research in a KAUST lab in Thuwal, Saudi Arabia. KAUST lists more than 100 faculty-led projects across science, engineering, computing, AI, marine science, energy and the environment; you pick a project and work with that faculty member's group, with access to KAUST's core laboratories.

It is fully funded: a USD 1,000 monthly stipend, a private bedroom and bathroom on campus, return airfare, campus facilities and social and cultural activities. Applications are accepted all year with flexible start and end dates, and there is no application fee. Many students use it as a route into KAUST's fully funded MS and PhD programmes.

You need to be at least a third-year undergraduate or a master's student (recent graduates within a year also qualify), with a GPA of at least 3.5/4 and proof of English proficiency. You apply to one project at a time with transcripts, a statement of purpose, a CV, your passport and one faculty recommendation.
highlights: USD 1,000/month stipend, flights and private campus housing
100+ faculty-led STEM projects; flexible 2–6 month duration
Rolling admissions and no application fee
kaust-visiting-student-research-program.eligibility: Third-year or higher undergraduates and master's students of any nationality (or graduates within one year of the start date). Minimum GPA 3.5/4 or equivalent. English proficiency proof (IELTS, TOEFL, PTE, Cambridge C1/C2 or Duolingo) unless exempt. Current PhD students and KAUST students/alumni are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Browse the VSRP project list on the KAUST admissions site and choose one project.
Click Apply on that project page (one application at a time).
Upload English transcripts, a statement of purpose, CV and passport (6+ months validity).
Name one faculty recommender; KAUST contacts them directly.
Wait for a decision (KAUST decides on a rolling basis).
kaust-visiting-student-research-program.costs: Free to apply. Fully funded: USD 1,000 monthly stipend, private housing, return airfare and campus access.

mbzuai-global-research-internship-2027.about:
MBZUAI, the world's first graduate university dedicated to artificial intelligence, runs a four-week research internship on its Abu Dhabi campus each summer. Previously called the Undergraduate Research Internship Program (UGRIP), it has been renamed the MBZUAI Global Research Internship Program (MGRIP) and widened to undergraduate and master's students from around the world. The 2027 edition runs 7 June to 2 July 2027.

Interns join small teams working on faculty-led projects across machine learning, computer vision, natural language processing, robotics and related areas, attend lectures and workshops, and present their results at the end. Past UGRIP cohorts were hosted on campus with travel and accommodation provided; check the MGRIP page for the 2027 funding terms. The 2027 project list is due to be published in November 2026.

Applications open 1 January 2027 and close 28 February 2027, with decisions by 2 April. In the previous cycle applicants needed a STEM-related major, a CGPA of at least 3.5/4 and an approved English test score. It is a strong option for students considering MBZUAI's fully funded MSc and PhD programmes.
highlights: Four weeks of hands-on AI research on MBZUAI's Abu Dhabi campus
Open worldwide to undergraduate and master's students
Pathway towards MBZUAI's fully funded graduate programmes
mbzuai-global-research-internship-2027.eligibility: Undergraduate and master's students from any country. The previous cycle required a STEM-related major, CGPA 3.5/4 or higher and an approved English test; confirm 2027 requirements on the MGRIP page.
how_to_apply: Check the 2027 project list on the MGRIP page (released November 2026).
Prepare transcripts, CV, English test score and statement.
Apply online between 1 January and 28 February 2027 (5 pm GST).
Receive a decision by 2 April 2027.
mbzuai-global-research-internship-2027.costs: No tuition. Earlier editions covered travel and on-campus accommodation for interns; confirm the 2027 package on the official page.

mawhiba-national-gifted-olympiad-ibdaa-2.about:
Mawhiba's National Gifted Olympiad is the main gateway for Saudi school students into international science competitions. It has two tracks under one framework. Ibdaa, the research track, is a national science and engineering fair: students submit an individual research project, attend training lectures, go through online judging, present at regional exhibitions and, if they qualify, at the national exhibition, which selects the Saudi delegation to the Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF).

Nasmu, the science track, is an olympiad pathway in mathematics, science, informatics (C++), physics, chemistry and biology. Students sit an electronic test, a national-team test, then training camps with central tests and finals; finalists join Saudi national-team preparation for international olympiads (IMO, IPhO, IChO, IBO, IOI, AI and more). Saudi students compete in more than 29 international olympiads and fairs through this route.

Both tracks are free, and participation does not affect the regular school track. Training days, exhibitions and tests are in person. Ibdaa winners receive prizes, and every finalist receives a certificate.
highlights: Free; the official pathway to ISEF and international science olympiads for Saudi students
Two tracks: Ibdaa (individual research projects) and Nasmu (olympiad subjects)
Training lectures, regional and national exhibitions, national-team camps
mawhiba-national-gifted-olympiad-ibdaa-2.eligibility: Ibdaa: Saudi nationals in intermediate or secondary general education, aged 11–20, one individual project each. Nasmu: students from first intermediate to first secondary grade (subject-specific), registered through their school coordinator. In person in Saudi Arabia.
how_to_apply: Log in to the Mawhiba website or app and confirm your profile.
For Ibdaa, register through the National Gifted Olympiad service before the deadline and submit your project and documents.
For Nasmu, register through your school's olympiad coordinator.
Attend the training lectures and the electronic tests or judging.
Qualifiers present at central exhibitions or attend national-team camps.
mawhiba-national-gifted-olympiad-ibdaa-2.costs: Free registration. In-person attendance at training days and exhibitions is required (travel within Saudi Arabia at your own cost unless Mawhiba states otherwise).

bebras-mawhiba-2026.about:
Bebras is one of the world's largest informatics and computational-thinking challenges, run in more than 60 countries. Mawhiba organises the Saudi edition, Bebras Mawhiba, as a fully remote test for students from grade 3 of primary through grade 3 of secondary school.

The test has 10 interactive problems, each with four levels of increasing difficulty (maximum 400 points). Problems test logic, algorithms, patterns and data reasoning rather than coding, so no programming background is needed, and it can be taken in Arabic or English. Students get one attempt, see results immediately after the test, and winners receive medals delivered via their regional education departments.

It is an accessible first competition for younger students and a good warm-up for the informatics olympiad track. The official site has a Bebras library with sample problems for practice.
highlights: Remote, in Arabic or English, no coding needed
10 interactive problems with four difficulty levels
Medals for winners; good entry point to informatics olympiads
bebras-mawhiba-2026.eligibility: Students from grade 3 primary to grade 3 secondary enrolled in general education inside Saudi Arabia (any nationality).
how_to_apply: Log in to the Bebras Mawhiba website (bebrasksa.org) and confirm your profile.
Register through the service system and accept the terms.
Pay the SAR 60 contribution before 26 November 2026.
Practise with the Bebras library, then take the test on the scheduled date.
bebras-mawhiba-2026.costs: SAR 60 guardian contribution (Apple Pay, mada, Visa, Mastercard).

mawhiba-tamayuz-elite-universities-2027.about:
Tamayuz (Excellence) is Mawhiba's flagship programme for getting Saudi high-school students into the world's most selective universities, mainly top-ranked US institutions. It targets students in the second year of secondary school and runs through the application season: SAT training, university essay-writing workshops, help completing applications and forms, and individual advising sessions, with an emphasis on STEM majors.

The programme itself provides training only. After admission, students apply to partner sponsors such as the Ministry of Education, KAUST (via KGSP) and Aramco for scholarships to fund their studies. A separate six-week Tamayuz Preparation course for first-year secondary students focuses on the SAT and is optional.

Applicants need averages of at least 90% in grade 9 and grade 10, 90%+ in maths, computer science and science, and an SAT of 1000+ or IELTS Academic 6.5 / TOEFL iBT 80 (SAT holders get priority), plus a personal interview in English. Non-Saudi students can register to benefit from the training content.
highlights: SAT, essay and application coaching for top US universities
Links to sponsorship from the Ministry of Education, KAUST and Aramco after admission
Individual advising and STEM-major guidance
mawhiba-tamayuz-elite-universities-2027.eligibility: Second-year secondary (grade 11) students in Saudi Arabia with 90%+ averages in grades 9 and 10 and in maths/CS/science, plus SAT 1000+ or IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL 80, and a successful interview. Non-Saudis may register to benefit from the training.
how_to_apply: Log in to the Mawhiba website and confirm your profile.
Register through the Tamayuz service (registration.mawhiba.sa/Tamayuz).
Upload grade 9 and grade 10 certificates plus your SAT or English test report.
Book and pass the English interview once you become a "candidate".
Pay the contribution after acceptance.
mawhiba-tamayuz-elite-universities-2027.costs: SAR 4,600 for Mawhiba students (Saudi or Saudi mother, score 1400+ on the Mawhiba scale) and SAR 19,550 for others, each including a refundable SAR 1,150 deposit. Fee exemptions possible with documents.

mawhiba-gifted-identification-test-2026.about:
The Mawhiba Multiple Mental Abilities Test is the entry point to almost every Mawhiba programme. It is delivered with the National Center for Assessment (Qiyas/ETEC) at test centres across Saudi Arabia, in Arabic or English, at three levels: grades 3–5, grades 6–8 and grades 9–10. Each student can sit the test once per level.

Scores range from 1,000 to 2,000 and stay valid until you move to the next level. Each Mawhiba programme sets its own threshold: Mawhiba classes in partner schools, summer enrichment programmes (such as the Universal Enrichment Program at Saudi universities), the advanced science and maths programme and the Tamayuz top-university preparation programme. Students who do not reach a threshold can still join Mawhiba competitions and retake at the next level.

If you are a student in Saudi Arabia interested in gifted programmes, this test is the first step.
highlights: Unlocks Mawhiba classes, enrichment and university-prep programmes
Arabic or English; three age levels
Free if nominated by your teacher
mawhiba-gifted-identification-test-2026.eligibility: Students from grade 3 of primary to grade 1 of secondary at schools in Saudi Arabia. One attempt per level. Some follow-on programmes are limited to Saudi nationals or children of Saudi mothers.
how_to_apply: Self-nominated students log in to the Sadeed platform (sadeed.etec.gov.sa) and choose the Mawhiba Multiple Mental Abilities Test.
Choose a test venue and date and accept the terms.
Pay the SAR 200 fee before 28 December 2026.
Teacher-nominated students confirm attendance and choose a venue on the Qiyas site (no fee).
mawhiba-gifted-identification-test-2026.costs: SAR 200 for self-nominated students; free for teacher-nominated students.

kaust-academy-hssp-2027.about:
The High School Summer Program (HSSP) is KAUST Academy's residential STEM programme for high-achieving secondary students. Each track starts with about two weeks at KAUST in Thuwal and finishes with a week at a UK university. The KAUST–Oxford track (9–30 July 2027) is broad and interdisciplinary: mathematics, programming, physics, chemistry, biology, leadership and collaborative research projects. The KAUST–Cambridge track (about 30 July – 22 August 2027) focuses on advanced mathematics, programming and computational thinking, and innovation projects.

The fee covers return flights, ground transport, accommodation (shared rooms at KAUST, single rooms in the UK, separate housing for boys and girls), full board, tuition, trips, campus facilities and healthcare. After the summer, participants get remote SAT preparation (September–October 2027), an on-campus college admissions camp at KAUST in November 2027 and mentoring on US and UK university applications through March 2028.

Applicants must be at least 15 by the UK flight date. A parent or guardian submits the application between 1 November and 31 December 2026; shortlisted students are interviewed online about their academic interests and readiness. It is expensive, but it combines two world-class campuses with structured university-admissions support.
highlights: Two weeks at KAUST plus a week at Oxford or Cambridge
All-inclusive: flights, housing, meals, tuition and trips
Follow-up SAT prep and US/UK admissions mentoring to March 2028
kaust-academy-hssp-2027.eligibility: High-school students aged at least 15 by the UK flight date. The page does not set a nationality restriction; the application is made by a parent or legal guardian. Teaching in English.
how_to_apply: A parent or guardian completes the online application on the KAUST Academy HSSP page (opens 1 November 2026).
Pay the non-refundable SAR 200 application fee by 31 December 2026.
Watch for interview instructions by email within a week of the deadline.
Attend the online interview if shortlisted.
kaust-academy-hssp-2027.costs: Application fee SAR 200. Programme fee SAR 35,000 (Oxford track) or SAR 40,000 (Cambridge track), excluding VAT, covering flights, transport, accommodation, meals, tuition, trips and healthcare. No financial aid is listed.

kaust-mathematics-competition-2027.about:
The KAUST Mathematics Competition is a national olympiad-style contest run by KAUST Academy for students in grades 6 to 11 at schools across Saudi Arabia, open to both Saudi nationals and residents. Phase 1 is a two-hour, in-person written test on 23 January 2027 at around 50 centres nationwide (24 multiple-choice questions for grades 6–7 and 8–9, 30 for grades 10–11). Questions are in Arabic and English, and calculators are not allowed.

The top 250 students advance to Phase 2, a three-day event at KAUST in Thuwal on 2–4 April 2027 with a four-hour written-response final, enrichment activities and an awards ceremony. KAUST covers domestic airfare, transport, accommodation and meals for finalists.

Winners receive prizes and free places on KAUST Academy programmes, and first-place winners in grades 8–9 and 10–11 earn an exclusive summer training camp at the University of Cambridge. It is an affordable, high-quality maths competition and a good stepping stone towards national olympiad teams and KAUST's pre-college programmes.
highlights: Open to Saudi nationals and residents in grades 6–11
Fully funded three-day final at KAUST for the top 250
Top winners get a summer camp at the University of Cambridge
kaust-mathematics-competition-2027.eligibility: Students in grades 6–11 at schools in Saudi Arabia; Saudi nationals and Saudi residents.
how_to_apply: Open the KMC page on the KAUST Academy website and click "Apply now".
Pay the SAR 100 non-refundable fee by 12 December 2026 (registration is confirmed automatically).
Check the test-centre announcement after registration closes.
Sit Phase 1 on 23 January 2027; qualifiers attend the KAUST final on 2–4 April 2027.
kaust-mathematics-competition-2027.costs: SAR 100 registration fee. Final-round costs (domestic flights, transport, accommodation, meals) are covered by KAUST.

kaust-academy-steps-2027.about:
STEPs is KAUST Academy's college-preparation programme for Saudi high-school students aiming at the world's leading universities, including the 30 universities on the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques Scholarship (Arruaad) list. The 2026/27 cycle combines an online component in June 2027, an in-person summer programme at KAUST from 2 July to 11 August 2027, and further online sessions in September–November 2027.

During the summer, mornings are spent on advanced mathematics, programming and SAT training, and afternoons on mentor-guided group projects in a subject of your choice. There is also a speaker series, university-preparation and professional-development lectures, and extracurricular activities on KAUST's Red Sea campus.

Tuition and participation are free, including accommodation and meals during in-person periods; only a SAR 200 application fee applies. Selection is by a 90-minute maths and science admissions test on 19 December 2026 and a personal interview. There is no minimum GPA, but you must be a Saudi national currently in grade 10.
highlights: Free, including six weeks on campus at KAUST with housing and meals
Advanced maths, programming, SAT training and mentored projects
Aimed at admission to top global universities and Arruaad scholarship pathway

khalifa-university-ai-winter-camp-2026.about:
Khalifa University's Department of Computer Science runs an AI Winter Camp for high-school students during the December school break. The 2026 edition takes place 14–18 December 2026 on KU's main campus in Abu Dhabi and combines lectures, workshops and group projects using real AI tools.

The syllabus covers core AI concepts (machine learning, deep learning, neural networks and natural language processing), applications in healthcare, education and transport, AI for sustainability and social challenges, and career paths in AI, data science, robotics and automation. Students build and train their own machine-learning models, network with KU researchers and receive a certificate of participation.

The camp is free for selected participants, with lunch and snacks provided; bring a laptop. It is aimed at grade 10–12 students with strong science and maths grades and a real interest in AI. Applicants register online (via KU and ADEK channels) and must pass an entry interview. It is a short, free way to get university-level AI exposure and see one of the region's top-ranked engineering universities from the inside.

khalifa-university-job-shadowing-2026.about:
Khalifa University's Job Shadowing programme gives secondary students a short, practical look at what studying and working in science, technology, engineering and medicine involves. Each cohort of up to 25 students spends two or three days on KU's main campus in Abu Dhabi, meeting faculty, touring research labs and joining hands-on sessions; in 2025, 109 students took part, including a medicine and health-sciences track.

It is free for selected participants, with materials, lunch and snacks provided and a certificate of participation at the end. The programme runs in cohorts across the year, so it suits students exploring which STEM major to choose before university applications.

Only school counsellors can apply on behalf of students, so ask your school's careers or university counsellor to contact KU Outreach.
